long_biography.plain_text:
Alfa Romeos gave David Hart his first business arena. Trading cars sharpened his feel for machinery and dealmaking before he bought a warehouse in Rotterdam's Waalhaven. That property became the foundation of DHG. The company developed a model of building large distribution centres at its own risk, then selling or retaining them as market conditions changed.

Motorsport developed alongside the property business rather than after it. Hart raced internationally in GT cars and prototypes, making four starts in the Le Mans 24 Hours over an eleven-season span. Through DHG Racing he later concentrated on historic machinery, winning major Goodwood races in cars from his collection and competing with his son Olivier.
